Key Research Thinking Patterns: Thermodynamic Formalism for Metric Construction: Utilizing spectral gap properties of transfer operators on tower spaces to prove real-analyticity of pressure functions and Hausdorff dimensions, thereby defining non-degenerate path metrics (e.g., Weil-Petersson type) on stable components of polynomial moduli spaces.

Simultaneous Uniformization via Quasi-Conformal Methods: Applying the measurable Riemann mapping theorem and quasiconformal surgery to establish simultaneous uniformization theorems for quasi-Blaschke products, analogous to Bers' theorem for quasi-Fuchsian groups, to analyze the complex analytic structure of moduli spaces.

Spectral Analysis of Multiplier Correlations: Constructing Manhattan curves for pairs of hyperbolic rational maps and holomorphic endomorphisms to characterize the convexity and real-analyticity of these curves, linking them directly to the correlation number of multiplier spectra and volume dimensions of Julia sets.

Topological Obstruction via Fixed Point Analysis: Employing fixed point analysis of homeomorphisms and study of hyper-elliptic involutions to demonstrate the non-realizability of compactly supported mapping class groups for infinite type surfaces (e.g., plane minus a Cantor set) as subgroups of their homeomorphism groups.
Summary Description: Yan Mary He specializes in the intersection of geometric topology, complex dynamics, and thermodynamic formalism. Her research constructs natural path metrics on moduli spaces of rational maps and Blaschke products by leveraging the spectral properties of transfer operators and the real-analyticity of Hausdorff dimensions. She extends Sullivan's Dictionary by establishing simultaneous uniformization theorems for quasi-Blaschke products and analyzing Manhattan curves to correlate multiplier spectra with geometric invariants. Additionally, she addresses foundational problems in geometric topology, such as the generalized Nielsen realization problem for big mapping class groups of infinite type surfaces, using fixed point analysis to identify topological obstructions. Her work bridges dynamical systems and hyperbolic geometry, providing rigorous metric structures and rigidity results for complex dynamical systems.
